title: YOSHIKI Reflects on Music, Life, Legacy & His New Collaboration ‘Forever Love (Live)’ With Josh Groban: Interview
summary: Billboard JAPAN sat down with YOSHIKI to talk about how the collaboration came together and what's next.
body: YOSHIKI and Josh Groban ‘s collaborative recording of “Forever Love (Live)” was released for streaming worldwide on Aug. 28. The ballad, originally released in 1996 as X JAPAN’s 14th single, gets a new rendition, one born from a live performance which the two artists gave together at YOSHIKI CLASSICAL 2026 IN LOS ANGELES AT WALT DISNEY CONCERT HALL “VIOLET NIGHT” on July 17, 2026. Billboard JAPAN sat down with YOSHIKI to talk about how the collaboration came together, the raw emotions behind the original song, his ongoing commitment to philanthropy and what’s next. Could you explain what led to Josh Groban singing “Forever Love” with you, and then to releasing the song? I first met Josh at an event during the Sundance Film Festival in Park City in 2016, when the documentary “WE ARE X” premiered there. I’ve spent over half my life living in LA, so when I put on YOSHIKI CLASSICAL 2026 IN LOS ANGELES , I thought it would be good for the show to include friends that I had a personal connection with. This year is the 30th anniversary of the release of “Forever Love,” and I had this intuitive feeling that if Josh sang it, it would turn out amazi…

title: Kroi Talks New Song ‘SPIN’ & the Creative Journey Intersecting With the Chaos of ‘JoJo’
summary: Talking with the band revealed the relentless spirit of inquiry and creative urge behind "SPIN."
body: Kroi’s new song “SPIN” was written as the opener for the anime Steel Ball Run: JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure . A rousing melody and beat that evoke the American Old West, where the story is set, blend with Kroi’s signature chaotic funkiness, resulting in a highly original and exhilarating track. The song took off on streaming right after release, including the U.S. and debuted at No. 44 on Billboard’s Hot Rock & Alternative Songs chart (dated Oct. 10, 2026), the band’s first-ever entry on a Billboard U.S. chart. Talking with the band revealed the relentless spirit of inquiry and creative urge behind it — an attempt to depict a new world no one has ever seen by digging into cultures closely tied to the band, from the anime song, a uniquely Japanese form of pop, to The Ventures, part of vocalist Leo Uchida’s roots. Drummer Hidetomo Masuda was unfortunately absent due to illness, but the remaining four members shared the story behind the making of “SPIN.” Your new song “SPIN” is the opening theme for the anime Steel Ball Run: JoJo’s Bizarre Adventure . title: Assigning tasks to Gemini just got a little easier
summary: Google's downplaying Spark branding in favor of a new 'Task' button.
body: TL;DR Gemini Spark now lives on the app’s home screen on mobile. Spark is accessible through a new button labeled Task. Chat and task history has also been reorganized. Gemini’s Spark feature that can automate your digital tasks is getting easier to access. A recent update adds a Task button to the Gemini app’s home screen, simplifying the process to set Gemini to work on all your mundane internet grunt work. As noted by 9to5Google , Gemini Spark has graduated from the app’s navigation drawer to prime real estate right on its home screen. It’s also ditched the Spark branding in the UI, with the new button reading “Task.”

title: Samsung Galaxy phones can’t tell if they’re connected to Bluetooth or not
summary: The Samsung Galaxy's volume slider is mixing up its connected device icons.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Samsung Galaxy phone users are experiencing a strange bug affecting the volume panel. When playing audio through the phone’s speakers, a Bluetooth icon appears at the bottom of the slider. Instead of an earbud icon, a speaker icon reportedly appears when earbuds are connected. You may not always notice it, but the volume slider on your Galaxy phone conveys more information than just the volume level. Whether you’re listening to music through your earbuds or blasting it through your Bluetooth speakers, there will be a little symbol at the bottom of the panel that lets you know what your phone is connected to. However, a new bug is causing issues with this indicator. Samsung Galaxy phone users ( 1 , 2 , 3 ) are experiencing a strange glitch affecting the volume panel. When playing audio through the handset’s speakers, a Bluetooth icon appears at the bottom of the slider. That should not be happening, as it suggests the phone is connected to a Bluetooth device even though it is disconnected. Users also report seeing a speaker icon instead of an earbud icon when their earbuds are connected.

title: Pixel users report frustrating screen animation bugs after Android 17 QPR1 update
summary: The issue is primarily being reported by Pixel 10 users.
body: TL;DR September’s Android 17 QPR1 release has caused a problem for Pixel owners who are experiencing incorrect animations on the home and recent apps screens. The issue seems like it might be limited to the Pixel 10 series. Google is aware of the problem and is investigating it. For a phone that’s at the forefront of Android developments, the Pixel is also a leader when it comes to bugs. The latest has arrived with September’s Android 17 QPR1 release . Pixel owners are registering an issue they’re having with incorrect animations on the home and recent apps screens ever since the update. Over on Reddit’s Pixel sub, our original poster shares that when they try to return to the launcher from an app on their Pixel 10 Pro XL, instead of the downward animation they previously would get, the app goes to the recent apps screen and then slides away to the right. Additionally, they note that when they go to the recent apps screen from within an app, the app icon sometimes gets stuck on the screen while the recent apps screen opens behind it.

title: Survey reveals Kindle readers aren’t buying Amazon’s pricey page-turning solution
summary: Amazon's new Kindle Page-Turn Cover promises extra convenience, but our readers have strong opinions about the price tag.
body: Credit: Amazon Physical page-turn buttons might seem like a pretty basic feature for an e-reader , but Amazon has spent years leaving them off its Kindle lineup. The company has given bookworms a way to bring them back with its latest devices, although it’s charging a hefty premium for the privilege. We recently asked readers whether they’d be willing to pay $80 for this convenience, and the results suggest Amazon might have misread the room. As my colleague Dhruv Bhutani explained in his recent look at the 2026 Kindle refresh , Amazon’s new Page-Turn Cover adds physical buttons to the e-reader through a magnetic connection. The catch is that it costs $80 and it only works with the Signature Editions of the Kindle Paperwhite and Colorsoft, which already cost $250 and $320, respectively. That makes $330 the minimum entry price if you want physical buttons on a new Kindle. We wanted to know whether you thought this was fair enough, or if perhaps Amazon should have just included this functionality as part of the deal.

The company will now offer an Enhanced Protection mode in Google Messages along with call-forwarding warnings. Google is also bringing Scam Detection for chat notifications to a ton of other Android phones globally. There’s no shortage of security-focused features in Android, including Advanced Protection Mode , Scam Detection for calls and texts, and theft detection . Opt in to this mode and you’ll activate Scam Detection with “secure” cloud analysis, warnings for links from unfamiliar numbers, and malicious link protection powered by Gemini Nano.

title: Survey confirms the ‘hidden’ part of this Pixel hidden gem
summary: We knew Pixel VIPs was underrated, and you proved just how much.
body: TL;DR Nearly 79% of respondents to our recent poll said they had never heard of Pixel VIPs, despite the feature being over a year old. Only 7% said they use Pixel VIPs regularly, while 14% expressed interest in trying it out. Google recently upgraded Pixel VIPs with one-tap calling and messaging, notification badges, and a redesigned interface. Google first introduced a seamless way to give some of your favorite contacts elevated importance and permissions with the June 2025 Pixel Feature Drop . Called Pixel VIPs , the feature essentially let you give some contacts a spot on your home screen through a dedicated widget. Fast forward to last month, and Google rolled out improvements with Pixel VIPs 2.0. However, despite the upgrade, a large portion of our users don’t even know this exists at all. We recently ran a poll asking our users whether they use Pixel VIPs, and a whopping majority of 1,545 respondents said they’ve never heard of the feature.

title: Samsung’s Good Lock team confirms widget text and volume slider bugs
summary: If you're also experiencing these problems, you can rest easy knowing Samsung is working on a fix.
body: Credit: Ryan Haines / Android Authority TL;DR Good Lock users are reporting a problem with text size when reducing the size of widgets and icons. Samsung states that it is searching for ways to solve the problem. The team has also confirmed a bug where different volume levels are displayed on the Quick Settings panel and the volume panel. One of the nice things about Galaxy phones is how customizable they can be. With the Good Lock app, you can modify almost your entire experience, from adding custom styles and animations to notifications to adjusting the layout and spacing of tiles in Quick Settings. However, as with any software, a bug can ruin the experience. Unfortunately, there are two bugs that are currently annoying Good Lock users. The first bug is connected to the Good Lock module known as Home Up. If you’re not familiar with Home Up, it allows you to reposition apps anywhere on the screen, resize widgets, and more. The problem in question deals with resizing widgets. As one user explains , when they reduce the size of icons and widgets, the text becomes proportional in size. The text can get so small that it becomes illegible.

summary: They could be sticking with a Galaxy S23-era selfie cam.
body: TL;DR The Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra are rumored to come with an upgraded front-facing camera. A new rumor says that the S27 and S27 Plus won’t receive the same upgrade. That would make the S27 the fourth consecutive Galaxy S generation to leverage the same 12-megapixel sensor. Galaxy S27 season is creeping up: Samsung’s next non-folding flagships should be here in just a few months. We’ve already seen leaks about the phones’ hardware design , cameras , and other specs . Today, a new camera rumor has popped up, and it’s not great news. Galaxy Club reports that, in contrast with the Galaxy S27 Pro and Galaxy S27 Ultra, the two lesser models will stick with the same front-facing camera as this year’s Galaxy S26 series. That’s a 12-megapixel shooter that’s been unchanged for several generations.

title: Your Android phone can now shut down or restart your PC
summary: Not around your PC to restart or shut it down? The Link to Windows app now lets you do it remotely.
body: TL;DR The Link to Windows app is getting new power control options, letting users remotely shut down, restart, or put their computer to sleep. These key functions were first revealed in a report last month and now appear to be rolling out through the latest Link to Windows beta. In addition to letting you control key power options, the new menu in the Link to Windows app also lets you finish updates before you restart or shut down the PC. Microsoft’s Link to Windows is a useful utility app that lets you remotely access certain phone functions on your Windows computer. It currently lets you access phone calls, messages, photos, and transfer files between your desktop and a linked Android phone. We recently learned that Microsoft is adding the ability to remotely shut down , restart, or put your computer to sleep . These functions are now officially rolling out in the Link to Windows app. While Link to Windows currently lets you lock your computer, the version 1.26101.103.0 beta adds additional controls for common actions.

title: Yikes: Google let a fake Chrome app on the Play Store, and it got over 100,000 downloads
summary: Sideloading is risky, but apparently so is the Play Store.
body: TL;DR A fake Google Chrome app with over 100,000 downloads was available on the Play Store. The app, from a developer named “Hizbartech,” even paid its way to the top of the search results for “Chrome.” Google has since removed the app, but it raises questions about the Play Store’s review and ad practices. Google talks a big game about trying to keep the Android ecosystem safe and secure. The company recently started cracking down on sideloading apps because malicious actors can easily create fake apps and trick users into installing them. Instead, Google wants users to install apps directly from the Play Store. The idea is that installing apps from the Play Store pretty much guarantees you won’t install a fake or malicious app. However, Google doesn’t seem to be doing a stellar job of keeping the Play Store safe, either.

title: Google is selling Pixel and Samsung phones inside the Play Store
summary: Google really wants you to buy hardware from the Play Store.

Google’s support page says that devices listed on the Google Store will show up in the Play Store. Google is no stranger to using the Play Store to sell hardware. Earlier this year, the company started showing banners for the Galaxy Watch 8 inside the Play Store . However, if you thought that was all Google would do, you were wrong. Google has quietly added a new “Shop devices” option in the Play Store’s account switcher (h/t Telegram user catat2am). The tip we originally received showed Samsung devices like the Galaxy S26 Ultra and the Galaxy S26 alongside Google devices.

title: PSA: Google is silently linking your phone number across all signed-in accounts
summary: Android’s phone number verification setting is opt-out, and links your number across every Google account on your device.
body: Credit: Brady Snyder / Android Authority TL;DR Google now automatically verifies and attaches your phone number to every Google account signed in on your Android device without explicit prompts. Google updated its documentation between August and October 2025 to reflect this opt-out behavior, which links numbers across secondary, work, and alt profiles. Users can turn off “Verify phone numbers automatically” in their Android device’s Google settings page, but previously linked numbers must be manually removed from each Google account’s Personal Info page. Your Android phone is deeply integrated with a number of Google services, but a quiet background mechanism is currently causing a stir among users. A growing number of Android users are only now learning that Google automatically verifies and associates their phone number with every Google account logged into their device, without any explicit confirmation prompt. As spotted in a recent Reddit thread, users report receiving confirmation emails out of the blue from “noreply-phone-verification@google.com” stating that their phone number has been verified. title: The iPhone 18 Pro’s new camera feature is a sneaky trap for Android brands
summary: We've been here before.
body: One of the biggest talking points about the iPhone 18 Pro series is the mechanical variable-aperture lens on the primary rear camera. Apple is far from the first to market with this tech, but as we see time and again, Android brands will rush to copy this feature into upcoming flagships. In the interest of our collective wallets, Android OEMs should resist the knee-jerk impulse: without a substantially large imaging sensor to back it up, variable aperture adds unnecessary manufacturing costs and mechanical complexity for little real-world payoff.

title: I tried gaming on a Googlebook — here’s the good (and bad) news
summary: Intel-based Googlebooks are a clear step down from Snapdragon-powered models.
body: Credit: Hadlee Simons / Android Authority We’ve waited a while, but the first Googlebooks are finally on the market. These laptops run on a so-called Googlebook OS platform, touted as a hybrid of Android and Chrome OS. The big draws of Googlebooks are features like deep Gemini integration, Android app support, and the ability to stream apps from your phone. Can you actually play games and emulators on Googlebooks, though? That was one of the first thoughts I had when I realized I’d be getting a review unit. So, I thought it would be a good idea to find out.

title: Samsung is expanding One UI 9 with Android 17 to the oldest qualifying flagships
summary: Just days after Galaxy S24, the Galaxy S23 is starting to receive stable One UI 9.
body: Credit: Paul Jones / Android Authority TL;DR Stable One UI 9 has arrived for the Galaxy S23 series phones. The update is currently limited to users previously beta-testing One UI 9 on their Galaxy S23 in South Korea. Based on the rollout for other devices, the stable One UI 9 update for all users across different regions should be here in a week or two. Samsung started rolling out stable One UI 9 , based on Android 17, in late September. Over the past three or so weeks, several of Samsung’s older flagships — and even the latest Galaxy A series phone — have received the update. And now, it’s coming to even older devices. Based on a post in Samsung’s Community forums (via tipster Tarun Vats on X ), One UI 9 has seemingly started to roll out for Galaxy S23 users, just a couple of days after the Galaxy S24 series got its update in the US. The release is not available to all, but is currently limited to a smaller section of users who were previously beta testing One UI 9 on their Galaxy S23 devices. Furthermore, the release is currently limited to South Korea, Samsung’s home country.

title: Want to show an iPhone on TV? These are some of Apple’s ridiculous licensing rules
summary: We've known that bad guys can't use iPhones, but Apple's list of restrictions is really something.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR A Canadian TV show has reportedly switched from iPhones to Android phones due to Apple’s extensive list of requirements. Some of Apple’s demands include that no character can damage or destroy an iPhone, use a damaged model, or use an iPhone with a protective case. The production company is now mostly using Galaxy phones in lieu of iPhones. It’s not uncommon for TV shows and movies to use iPhones , but we’ve frequently heard that Apple doesn’t allow villains to be shown using its products. Now, a TV series has abandoned iPhones altogether in favor of Android devices due to Apple’s extensive list of rules. La Presse reports (via Mobile Syrup and iPhone in Canada ) that characters in Canadian series Antigang now use Android devices instead of iPhones. More specifically, the production is mostly using Samsung Galaxy phones .

title: Some Googlebooks OLED screens can’t display true black, but a fix is coming
summary: The engineering team has identified the cause and says a fix is already in the works.
body: TL;DR Some Googlebooks owners are reporting that their OLED displays show dark gray instead of true black once Googlebook OS loads. The issue appears across multiple Acer and Lenovo models, and the presence of proper blacks during boot/setup points to a software-related problem. Google says its engineering team has identified the root cause and is working to get a fix out very soon. Google has been moving quickly to sand down Googlebook OS’ rougher edges. Recent fixes have expanded Better Together features to Samsung phones , while the company has clarified Intel app compatibility and promised to expand HDR playback to Googlebooks that launched without it. But new hardware rarely gets every wrinkle ironed out at once, and Google is already chasing another conspicuous problem: some Googlebooks OLED displays aren’t actually displaying black as black. Owners of several OLED-equipped Googlebooks have reported on Reddit that areas of the screen that should be completely black instead appear dark gray. The complaints span at least Acer and Lenovo models with different screen sizes, suggesting this isn’t simply one manufacturer shipping a questionable panel.

title: Gemini Skills rollout has hit a speed bump for some users
summary: And Google says it wants to ensure a "safe and reliable" rollout for high-stakes users.
body: Credit: Joe Maring / Android Authority TL;DR Google is delaying the rollout of Gemini skills for Workspace users. It says the rollout is on hold to ensure “safe and reliable” access for every enterprise user. Google hasn’t specified a rollout date, but says it will share an update when it is confirmed. Last month, Google confirmed its plans to sunset Gemini’s usage-specific Gems and replace them with skills. These skills are easier to set up, access, and invoke in any conversation , and they don’t force you to use them in an isolated environment like Gems did. With its announcement, Google has already started bringing skills to Gmail users , including those on Gemini’s free tiers. For enterprise users, however, Google set a later rollout date, and it has now been pushed back. Earlier, Google had promised that skills would start rolling out in the Gemini app for all Workspace users on October 13. However, last-minute changes have pushed that rollout date back indefinitely, Google confirmed in a blog post . It noted that the release has been “delayed” to ensure a “safe and reliable” rollout for skills. Google hasn’t added a new date, and it has scrubbed any previous mentions from it…

title: I tested the first phone with triple 200MP cameras — and resolution isn’t the best part
summary: 200MP on every camera sounds ridiculous. Then I tried OPPO’s Find X10 Pro Max.
body: Credit: Robert Triggs / Android Authority OPPO has quickly risen in my smartphone camera rankings, thanks to a solid blend of cutting-edge hardware and Hasselblad camera processing. This year’s OPPO Find X10 Pro Max ups the ante again with a triple 200-megapixel camera count — a first for the mobile industry. That said, the regular Find X10 sports a very capable, almost equally versatile triple-camera arrangement that you should keep an eye on as well. But don’t let the huge megapixel count distract you; the Find X10 Pro Max is a play for an all-around great camera phone. The main benefit is sensor matching, ensuring very similar levels of light capture, noise, and HDR performance, regardless of which of the three lenses you use. In theory, there’s no more noticeable color shift or noise introduction when switching between ultrawide and zoom capabilities, making the triple camera much closer to functioning as a single package without compromise.

title: Googlebook OS Magisk demo shows root access could be much easier than first thought
summary: It might not need specialized debug hardware after all.
body: Credit: Richard Priday / Android Authority TL;DR Magisk developer John Wu shared a video demonstrating full root access on Googlebook OS, seemingly without requiring host-machine tethering or specialized debug cables. Previously, there were concerns that rooting Googlebooks could need specialized debug cables to connect to host machines. Googlebook OS also broke Magisk’s single-primary-user assumptions, so a fix was in the works. Wu hasn’t released a step-by-step public guide or ready-to-use Magisk build for Googlebook OS just yet, but these could be right around the corner. Rooting Google’s new Googlebook laptops won’t be the headache power users were dreading. Magisk developer John Wu previously teased Magisk coming to Googlebook OS , and now the developer has shared a video demonstrating that full root access can be achieved. More impressively, the process looks to be on-device so far, without seemingly requiring specialized hardware or host-machine tethering. In a post on X , Wu wrote, “This is how you’ll root your Googlebook,” and shared a brief video that walks through the rooting workflow.

title: Googlebook OS just fixed one of its biggest early app annoyances
summary: Googlebooks can now turn practically any website into an app.
body: TL;DR Chrome 155 lets Googlebook users install any webpage as a web app, even if the site lacks an installable web manifest. Installed web apps can open in their own windows, appear in the app launcher, and be pinned to the taskbar or homescreen. The update also moves Chrome Settings into a separate tab and is rolling out through Google Play over the next few days. Googlebook OS is barely out of the starting gate, but early adopters have already given Google a fairly clear homework list . Apps have been one of the biggest talking points, from some Android apps behaving differently across hardware to major Google services running as web experiences instead of native Android apps. Google now appears to be moving quickly on some of that feedback, and its latest Chrome update addresses one particularly annoying limitation. With Chrome 155, Googlebook owners can install any webpage as a web app, even when the website wasn’t specifically designed to be installable. Previously, sites without the necessary web app manifest could only be saved as shortcuts that opened in regular browser tabs.

title: Google will pay you up to $20,000 for Chrome security bugs
summary: It's also adding new categories to the reward program.
body: TL;DR Google is quadrupling the base reward amount for reporting critical Chrome vulnerabilities. It is also introducing rewards of up to $20,000 for high-impact bugs. End-of-year awards will celebrate submissions from the community. Google has relied on vulnerability reports from security researchers alongside its own internal security teams to keep apps like Chrome secure against exploits. The company has made several changes to its Vulnerability Rewards Program (VRP) over the last few months, including reducing Chrome reward payouts in May and using AI to improve Chrome security in July. Now, the company is making further adjustments to the Chrome VRP. In a blog post, the company announces new reward amounts and categories. Google has quadrupled the base reward amount for memory corruption vulnerabilities to $2,000. Furthermore, reports for controlled reads and crashes in the browser, GPU, and network processes will now earn rewards of $4,000. Payouts for controlled writes, on the other hand, can go up to $20,000.

title: The iPhone Duo’s hinge cooling is the breakthrough Android foldables need
summary: Android foldables typically do not use the hinge as part of the thermal dissipation layer.
body: Credit: Aamir Siddiqui / Android Authority TL;DR Apple built a flexible graphite pipe into the iPhone Duo hinge to dissipate excess heat between the two chassis halves when folded. Combined with an unstacked A20 Pro SoC and vapor chamber, the active thermal hinge helps maintain peak performance for longer under heavy loads. Android foldables have used graphite sheets as part of the display stack or on the chassis on either side of the spine, but have not typically used the spine itself for cooling. Foldables have spent years balancing thinner profiles with flagship-grade SoCs and the resulting thermal dilemma. When unfolded, you have a large surface area that is great for thermal dissipation, but when folded, you create a thermal sandwich that suddenly has to work with only half the surface area. Apple appears to have solved this on its first foldable, the iPhone Duo , by incorporating the hinge into the phone’s cooling structure. According to a PCMag interview with Apple’s thermal and silicon engineering teams, the iPhone Duo’s fold itself was one of the device’s toughest thermal roadblocks. While book-style foldables are usually razor-thin when open, closing them stacks the chas…

title: ANBERNIC could be barred from selling its handhelds in the US
summary: The ESA is calling ANBERNIC handhelds "superfakes."
body: TL;DR ANBERNIC has been classified as a “superfake” by the Entertainment Software Association (ESA). The ESA has suggested that the US Trade Representative (USTR) include ANBERNIC on its list of “Notorious Markets.” This could potentially lead to ANBERNIC being barred from selling its hardware in the US. ANBERNIC has made quite a name for itself in the world of retro gaming thanks to its impressive selection of retro handhelds . However, if you were planning to buy a new ANBERNIC device, like the newly announced RG DDS , there’s some concerning news for you. The ESA has filed its suggestions for the USTR’s “Notorious Markets” list (spotted via Retrohandhelds ). Alongside sites and repackers that offer pirated game downloads, the association has called out ANBERNIC as one of the biggest threats to the gaming industry.
